# Implementing MVC ToDo App with PHP Symfony – Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This **medium-difficulty** course teaches you how to build a fully functional ToDo application using the **Symfony framework**, one of the most popular and enterprise-grade PHP frameworks. You'll learn the **Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern**, understand how Symfony's components work together, and develop practical full-stack web development skills.

**Who it's for:**
- PHP developers transitioning from procedural code to modern frameworks
- Backend engineers preparing for mid-level positions at companies using Symfony
- Full-stack developers wanting to understand professional-grade application structure

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
- **Architectural thinking**: MVC interviews often probe your understanding of separation of concerns
- **Real-world relevance**: Symfony is used by major corporations (Drupal, eZ Platform, Sylius)
- **Complete workflow**: You'll demonstrate ability to handle routing, database operations, form validation, and templating—core concepts tested in technical interviews
- **Best practices**: The course reinforces SOLID principles, dependency injection, and service-oriented architecture

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Symfony Framework Fundamentals** – Installation, configuration, project structure, and lifecycle
- **Routing & URL Generation** – Defining routes, HTTP methods, parameter handling, reverse routing
- **Controllers & Actions** – Request/response handling, data processing, redirects
- **Doctrine ORM & Entity Management** – Database modeling, migrations, repositories, relationships
- **Twig Templating Engine** – Template syntax, inheritance, loops, conditionals, filters
- **Form Handling & Validation** – Building forms, CSRF protection, data validation, error displays
- **Service Container & Dependency Injection** – Managing services, autowiring, custom services
- **Database Persistence & Relationships** – One-to-many, many-to-many, cascading operations
- **Authentication & Authorization** (optional advanced) – User roles, access control, security best practices

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Foundation & Setup (Tasks 1–12)**
1. Install Symfony CLI and create a new project
2. Understand the directory structure (`src/`, `templates/`, `config/`, `public/`)
3. Configure database connection (SQLite for local development)
4. Create your first controller and route
5. Generate a simple HTML response using Twig
6. Practice route parameters and variable binding
7. Set up a basic layout template with Twig inheritance
8. Create static pages (Home, About)
9. Handle GET/POST requests in controllers
10. Debug using Symfony's debug toolbar
11. Practice environment configuration (.env files)
12. Create your first service class

### **Phase 2: Data Modeling with Doctrine (Tasks 13–28)**
13. Create a `Task` entity with properties (id, title, description, completed, createdAt)
14. Generate a database table via migrations
15. Create additional entities if needed (Category, User)
16. Define entity relationships (Task belongs to Category)
17. Write a repository class to query tasks
18. Implement CRUD operations in a repository
19. Create fixtures to seed test data
20. Load fixtures into the database
21. Test entity relationships and lazy loading
22. Implement __toString() methods for debugging
23. Create database indexes for performance
24. Handle timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt) automatically
25. Write a custom repository method (e.g., `findCompletedTasks()`)
26. Practice entity validation annotations
27. Implement soft deletes or archiving logic
28. Test all database operations with basic assertions

### **Phase 3: Controllers & Routing (Tasks 29–41)**
29. Create a `TaskController` with index action (list all tasks)
30. Implement `show` action (display single task)
31. Create `new` action with form display
32. Build `create` action to persist new tasks
33. Implement `edit` action with form pre-population
34. Create `update` action to modify existing tasks
35. Build `delete` action with confirmation
36. Implement route naming and `path()` generation in templates
37. Handle 404 errors gracefully
38. Add success/error flash messages
39. Redirect after POST (PRG pattern)
40. Use `@ParamConverter` to auto-fetch entities
41. Implement filtering (e.g., show only incomplete tasks)

### **Phase 4: Forms & Validation (Tasks 42–52)**
42. Create a `TaskFormType` form class
43. Add text fields, textarea, checkbox for completion status
44. Implement form rendering in Twig template
45. Add CSRF token protection
46. Validate task title (required, min/max length)
47. Validate description (optional but if present, min length)
48. Create custom validation constraints
49. Display validation errors in the template
50. Implement conditional field validation
51. Handle file uploads (optional: attach images to tasks)
52. Test form submission with invalid data

### **Phase 5: Templating & UI (Tasks 53–61)**
53. Create a master `base.html.twig` layout
54. Extend layout in all task templates
55. Build a task list template with loops and conditionals
56. Create a detail view template for single task
57. Build a form template (new/edit)
58. Implement navigation bar with active link detection
59. Add Bootstrap or Tailwind CSS integration
60. Create error and success message templates
61. Implement pagination for task list

### **Phase 6: Advanced Features (Tasks 62–71)**
62. Add priority levels to tasks (enum or dropdown)
63. Implement task filtering by status
64. Create a search feature (find tasks by keyword)
65. Add sorting (by date, priority, completion status)
66. Implement soft delete with "delete" button
67. Create a dashboard showing task statistics
68. Add task categories and category filtering
69. Implement due dates with validation
70. Create an export feature (list tasks as JSON/CSV)
71. Write integration tests for your complete application

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Architectural Understanding**
- How MVC separates concerns (Model = Entity, View = Twig, Controller = Logic)
- Service container and dependency injection patterns
- Configuration management and environment-specific settings

### **Backend Development**
- Entity design and relationships (1:N, N:N)
- Query optimization with repositories and DQL
- Transaction handling and data consistency
- Migration management for schema changes

### **Request/Response Handling**
- HTTP method routing (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
- Form submission and CSRF protection
- Redirect patterns and flash messages
- Error handling and status codes

### **Template Engineering**
- Twig syntax: loops, conditionals, filters, macros
- Template inheritance and block overriding
- Dynamic HTML generation
- Working with collections in templates

### **Validation & Security**
- Form validation (built-in and custom constraints)
- Input sanitization
- CSRF token management
- Basic authentication setup

### **Problem-Solving Patterns**
- Debugging with Symfony's profiler
- Reading and interpreting error messages
- Reasoning about data flow through MVC layers
- Performance consideration (lazy loading, query optimization)

---

## Sample Problem Types

### **Problem Type 1: Entity Relationship & Query Logic**

**Description:**  
Design a `Task` entity with a relationship to a `Category` entity. Implement a repository method that retrieves all incomplete tasks within a specific category, ordered by priority (highest first), then by creation date (newest first).

**Code Sketch:**

```php
// src/Entity/Task.php
namespace App\Entity;

use Doctrine\ORM\Mapping as ORM;

#[ORM\Entity(repositoryClass: TaskRepository::class)]
class Task
{
    #[ORM\Id]
    #[ORM\GeneratedValue]
    #[ORM\Column]
    private ?int $id = null;

    #[ORM\Column(length: 255)]
    private string $title;

    #[ORM\Column(type: 'text', nullable: true)]
    private ?string $description = null;

    #[ORM\Column]
    private bool $completed = false;

    #[ORM\Column]
    private int $priority = 0; // 0=low, 1=medium, 2=high

    #[ORM\ManyToOne(targetEntity: Category::class)]
    #[ORM\JoinColumn(nullable: false)]
    private Category $category;

    #[ORM\Column(type: 'datetime_immutable')]
    private \DateTimeImmutable $createdAt;

    // Getters and setters...
}

// src/Repository/TaskRepository
